title: Browns, Todd Monken get special training camp visitor: Deion Sanders
content:
BEREA, Ohio — Cleveland Browns training camp is not yet open to the public, but Pro Football Hall of Famer and University of Colorado coach Deion Sanders scored a seat for Thursday’s practice — and a seat at the lunch table with Browns coach Todd Monken.

Though Sanders did not attend Browns camp last year when his son, Shedeur, was a rookie, Shedeur Sanders gave his father the OK this time around. Monken and Deion Sanders talked about everything from football to fatherhood before Thursday’s practice.

“It was really cool,” Monken said. “Deion Sanders, I mean, are you kidding me? Forget that it’s Shedeur’s dad. First of all, he did an unbelievable job with Shedeur, who’s a great kid. Deion was an amazing football player, a hell of a baseball player and is an amazing coach. Everything he’s accomplished … it was great (to talk with him).

“We just started telling stories. We got into NIL, and Jackson State, and Colorado and how we almost drafted Shedeur when I was in Baltimore and also what a great job Shedeur has done since I’ve been here as far as his development.”

The Browns are holding a quarterback competition this summer between Shedeur Sanders, who started the final seven games of his rookie season, and Deshaun Watson, who hasn’t played since 2024 and is in the final year of his contract.

Deion Sanders said on the Cleveland-based podcast “The Barbershop” last spring that he’d love to talk to Monken and called the first-year Browns coach “a straight shooter.” Deion Sanders greeted Monken with a playful bow at the conclusion of the team’s morning walk-through on Thursday.

As was the case in the spring, Monken is alternating his quarterbacks each day in camp, so Deion Sanders saw his son’s first day with the No. 1 offense in full training camp on Thursday. Monken hasn’t put a timetable on declaring a winner, saying only that the Browns need to have a starter by their Sept. 13 opener and that the best player will win the starting job.

Deion Sanders mostly watched practice alone from the bleachers. After practice, father and son shared a hug and a brief conversation after Shedeur Sanders took some extra post-practice throws, a standard part of his practice-day routine.
